card.name: Small words in old literary prose
card.fires_on: Small linking words (its, a, very, for, could, of, will) inside long, formal, 19th-century-style sentences, mostly in essays and architecture or history writing. It does not respond to drug-label text.

modes.label: Possessive or adjective before size
modes.description: Words like its or very right before a description of size or degree in architectural prose.
modes.example: The interior is very impressive, considering<< its>> very moderate size.

modes.label: Helper words after a subject
modes.description: Modal or auxiliary words such as could, cannot or will after a person subject in a reflective sentence.
modes.example: The Rabbi said he<< could>> detect the guilty party, if pen and

modes.label: Linking words in descriptions
modes.description: Prepositions or quantity words such as for, of or much inside a descriptive clause.
modes.example: a building remarkable<< for>> the great beauty of its proportions, and

card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in old-fashioned essay prose, not on any medical wording.
